three.js -- vendored
https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js
author: three.js authors (a collective, not a person -- see LICENSE)

Recorded at v4416.

RE-VENDORED 2026-09-14: r160 -> 0.185.1, backlog "vendor-three-r160-stale" (tools/ship/nextRounds.mjs).
Same version vendor/three-webgpu already re-vendored to on 2026-09-08 (see that directory's own
PROVENANCE.txt/README.md, used as this record's template) -- reusing tools/ship/three-probe.json's
already-vetted number rather than re-opening the version question for a second, unrelated vendor tree.
three.js's GitHub tags never adopted npm's semver scheme (r160, r180, etc. still resolve on GitHub;
there is no "0.185.1" tag), so there is no clean 1:1 mapping from the old "rNNN" pin to a git ref --
fetched instead from the npm registry tarball `three@0.185.1`
(https://registry.npmjs.org/three/-/three-0.185.1.tgz), which carries build/ and examples/jsm/
together under one immutable, versioned artefact. Same shape vendor/three-webgpu's own re-vendor used.

WHAT MOVED:
  - three.module.js (build/three.module.js) -- still the upstream ES module build, now a thin
    re-export shim over a NEW required file (see next line) rather than one self-contained file.
  - three.core.js (build/three.core.js, ~1.4 MB) -- NEW FILE, did not exist at r160. This is the
    split three.module.js -> three.core.js the backlog entry's own research found; without it every
    `import ... from "three"` throws at module-resolution time. vendor/three-webgpu already vendored
    its own copy of this same split file, which is how that research first confirmed the split was
    real and current.
  - jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js, jsm/loaders/{GLTFLoader,FBXLoader,KTX2Loader}.js,
    jsm/exporters/GLTFExporter.js, jsm/curves/{NURBSCurve,NURBSUtils}.js,
    jsm/libs/{fflate.module,ktx-parse.module,zstddec.module,meshopt_decoder.module}.js,
    jsm/libs/basis/{basis_transcoder.js,basis_transcoder.wasm,README.md}, jsm/utils/WorkerPool.js,
    jsm/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js -- each replaced with its 0.185.1 match from the same tarball's
    examples/jsm/ tree. See jsm/libs/basis/PROVENANCE.txt for that subdirectory's own license
    evidence (Apache-2.0, BinomialLLC, re-checked at the new file sizes rather than assumed
    unchanged).
  - jsm/utils/SkeletonUtils.js -- NEW FILE, did not exist in this directory at r160 (or at any prior
    vendoring). Upstream's GLTFLoader.js grew a static `import { clone } from '../utils/
    SkeletonUtils.js'` sometime between r160 and 0.185.1 that r160's GLTFLoader.js did not have --
    confirmed by grepping the old, still-on-disk-at-the-time r160 file's own `^import` lines, which
    named only BufferGeometryUtils.js. Without this file GLTFLoader.js's whole module graph fails to
    resolve (a browser `import()` 404s on the missing relative path and the error surfaces as
    "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module", not as anything naming SkeletonUtils directly) --
    caught the same way as the BufferGeometryUtils.js mistake below, by a real gate failure, not by
    reading the diff. It imports only from 'three' (AnimationClip, AnimationMixer, Matrix4,
    Quaternion, QuaternionKeyframeTrack, SkeletonHelper, Vector3, VectorKeyframeTrack -- all present
    in the new export set, checked), so it closes the same way NURBSCurve.js's own chain did.
  - jsm/math/ColorSpaces.js -- ANOTHER NEW FILE, same shape again: upstream's KTX2Loader.js grew
    `import { DisplayP3ColorSpace, LinearDisplayP3ColorSpace } from '../math/ColorSpaces.js'` between
    r160 and 0.185.1 that r160's KTX2Loader.js did not have. This is also the real explanation for two
    of the twelve "removed" symbols the API-break research below originally flagged --
    DisplayP3ColorSpace and LinearDisplayP3ColorSpace were never actually removed from three, they
    moved out of the top-level 'three' re-export into this examples-only submodule, which the export-
    diff method (comparing only build/three.module.js + build/three.core.js) could not see by
    construction. Found this time NOT by a gate failure -- gltfKtx2-selfcheck.mjs turned out not to
    dynamically `import()` KTX2Loader.js in a real browser at all (it calls gpu/gltfKtx2.js's
    ktx2Loader(null) directly in Node, which throws on the null-renderer guard before ever reaching
    the browser-only dynamic import, and its "page actually uses it" section only regex-scans
    glb_viewer.html's source text) -- so this gap would have shipped invisibly to that gate. Found
    instead by an exhaustive, second-pass scan: every `.js` file under vendor/three/jsm, every
    relative (`./` or `../`) import specifier in it, resolved against the filesystem and checked to
    exist -- zero missing, across all 23 files, only after this file was added. Corroborated
    independently by actually dynamically importing every vendored module (three.module.js,
    OrbitControls.js, GLTFLoader.js, FBXLoader.js, KTX2Loader.js, GLTFExporter.js,
    BufferGeometryUtils.js, SkeletonUtils.js, WorkerPool.js, NURBSCurve.js, NURBSUtils.js,
    ColorSpaces.js, fflate.module.js, ktx-parse.module.js, zstddec.module.js,
    meshopt_decoder.module.js, meshoptGltf.js, and vendor/draco/DRACOLoader.js) in a real headless
    Chromium page and confirming all 18 resolve with zero page errors. Imports only from 'three'
    (LinearTransfer, Matrix3, SRGBTransfer, SRGBColorSpace, ColorManagement -- all present, checked).
  - LICENSE -- copyright year advanced: "Copyright (c) 2010-2023 three.js authors" (r160) ->
    "Copyright © 2010-2026 three.js authors" (0.185.1), the same advance vendor/three-webgpu's own
    PROVENANCE.txt already recorded for this same upstream project.

*** A MISTAKE THIS RECORD USED TO PLAN, CAUGHT BY A GATE AND CORRECTED BEFORE SHIPPING -- NAMED HERE
RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED. *** The plan for this re-vendor, following the backlog entry's own research,
was to DROP jsm/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js as dead weight: a grep for callers OUTSIDE vendor/three
found none, matching the backlog's own claim. That grep was answering the wrong question.
GLTFLoader.js ITSELF -- at r160 AND at 0.185.1 both, confirmed by reading both files directly --
carries a static top-level `import { toTrianglesDrawMode } from '../utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js'`,
used for TRIANGLE_STRIP/TRIANGLE_FAN primitive-mode conversion. A caller inside vendor/three is still
a real caller; "zero callers outside vendor/three" was true and beside the point. Deleting the file
during this round broke GLTFLoader.js's module graph outright -- not only for glTF files using
strip/fan, but for every page that imports GLTFLoader at all, since an ES module import that 404s
fails the whole graph before any code runs. This was caught by tools/ship/dracoEncode-selfcheck.mjs
failing "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module" the first time this file was dropped and
verified against, not assumed safe from the research alone -- see that gate's own section 4. The file
was restored, re-vendored to 0.185.1 rather than left at r160, and ai-bridge/ensureThree.js's FILES
list keeps it. jsm/utils/TextureUtils.js is the one genuinely dropped file (see below) -- the
backlog's underlying instinct (this directory does carry real dead weight) was right about that one,
just not about both.

DROPPED, not re-vendored -- confirmed zero real callers, both outside AND inside vendor/three, checked
by grep across the whole tree AND by reading every vendored file's own `^import` lines, not assumed:
  - jsm/utils/TextureUtils.js -- zero callers anywhere, AND upstream at 0.185.1 no longer ships a
    matching examples/jsm/utils/TextureUtils.js at all -- confirmed directly in the fetched tarball,
    it has been split/renamed upstream into examples/jsm/utils/WebGLTextureUtils.js +
    WebGPUTextureUtils.js, a different API shape. Since nothing here called the old one, there was
    nothing to port to the new shape either way; deleted rather than left as dead weight. Unlike
    BufferGeometryUtils.js above, no vendored file's own import lines name it either (grepped
    directly), so this one drop stands as planned.
  ai-bridge/ensureThree.js's FILES list was updated: TextureUtils.js removed, three.core.js and
  jsm/utils/SkeletonUtils.js added, jsm/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js kept (not removed as first
  planned -- see above).

LEFT COMPLETELY ALONE -- not an upstream file:
  - jsm/libs/meshoptGltf.js is this engine's own code (wires EXT_meshopt_compression into
    GLTFLoader via setMeshoptDecoder), living here for co-location, not something the npm tarball has
    a matching path for. Not touched by this re-vendor. Its own logic was re-checked against the new
    GLTFLoader.js's actual setMeshoptDecoder API (unchanged -- see EVIDENCE below) rather than assumed
    to still apply.

REAL API-BREAK RESEARCH, not skipped: every top-level export present in the r160 build but absent
from the combined 0.185.1 build/three.module.js + build/three.core.js export set was enumerated by
diffing both builds' `export { ... }` statements, then grepped for across the entire engine tree
(HTML, JS, MJS; excluding this directory and vendor/three-webgpu). Twelve symbols were absent from
that top-level set (DisplayP3ColorSpace, Float64BufferAttribute, LinearDisplayP3ColorSpace,
LinearEncoding, LuminanceAlphaFormat, LuminanceFormat, P3Primaries, Rec709Primaries,
TwoPassDoubleSide, WebGL1Renderer, WebGLMultipleRenderTargets, _SRGBAFormat, sRGBEncoding) --
though, as the mistake note above this one records, two of those twelve (DisplayP3ColorSpace,
LinearDisplayP3ColorSpace) turned out to have MOVED to jsm/math/ColorSpaces.js rather than been
truly removed, which this export-diff method could not tell apart from an actual removal by
construction; the other ten really are gone. Exactly one real call site in the whole engine tree
used any of the twelve: view.html's `renderer.outputEncoding = THREE.sRGBEncoding` (both `.outputEncoding`
and `sRGBEncoding` are gone outright at 0.185.1 -- the r152-era deprecation shim that used to
translate this into `.outputColorSpace` with a console.warn has itself been removed) -- fixed in that
file to `renderer.outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace`, the modern equivalent, functionally a
no-op either way since `.outputColorSpace` already defaults to SRGBColorSpace. Every symbol every
vendored jsm/ file itself imports `from 'three'` (OrbitControls.js, GLTFLoader.js, FBXLoader.js,
KTX2Loader.js, GLTFExporter.js, NURBSCurve.js, NURBSUtils.js, SkeletonUtils.js,
BufferGeometryUtils.js -- 213 import names total across the nine files) was independently checked
present in the new export set: zero missing. OrbitControls'
base class is confirmed, by reading the actual vendored 0.185.1 file, to still be `class OrbitControls
extends Controls` where `Controls extends EventDispatcher` -- so `.addEventListener`/`.dispatchEvent`
call sites (voxearth.html's `controls.addEventListener("change", ...)`, the only such real call site
found) keep working. GLTFLoader/FBXLoader/KTX2Loader/GLTFExporter's public methods actually called
elsewhere in this tree (`setDRACOLoader`, `setKTX2Loader`, `setMeshoptDecoder`, `setTranscoderPath`,
`detectSupport`, `load`, `parse`, `parseAsync`, `.parse(scene, onDone, onError, {binary, animations,
includeCustomExtensions})`) were confirmed present with the same signatures by reading the vendored
files directly, not assumed stable. gpu/fbxLoad.js's harder-coded assumptions about FBXLoader's
internals (interpolation constants 2300/2301/2302, the `<model>.quaternion`/`.position`/`.scale`
track-naming convention, `new AnimationClip(name, -1, tracks)` triggering `resetDuration()`,
`PropertyBinding.sanitizeNodeName`) were each re-confirmed by reading the actual vendored
FBXLoader.js/three.core.js, not re-derived from memory of the old file.

EVIDENCE:
  - LICENSE reads "Copyright © 2010-2026 three.js authors" (advanced from "2010-2023" at r160).
  - three.module.js is the upstream's own ES module build; three.core.js is the file it now imports.
  - github.com/mrdoob/three.js appears 18 times in this directory.

*** AND THE MOST FREQUENT URL HERE IS STILL THE WRONG ONE. *** github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF appears
64 times -- the glTF loader/exporter cite the specification they implement, at both r160 and 0.185.1.
A scraper picking the commonest URL would still file three.js under KhronosGroup. That is why this
record exists as an attestation with its reasoning, and not as a scan.

NOT RE-VENDORED, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT: examples/jsm/postprocessing/ was never
vendored at r160 and still is not at 0.185.1 -- a pre-existing gap (ai-bridge/ensureSpark.js's own
header already documents it, for a different reason: spark's postprocessing imports resolve against
"/vendor/three/jsm/" and 404 there) that this round did not create and was not asked to close.

---- jsm/loaders/FBXLoader.js + its dependency closure -- vendored at r160, added for backlog
"fbx-ingest-has-no-loader" (tools/ship/nextRounds.mjs, commit 48488938): .fbx is treated as a
first-class recognized model extension throughout the tree but nothing ever parsed one. RE-VENDORED
2026-09-14 along with the rest of this directory (see above); the note this block used to carry --
that fetching FBXLoader.js from r160 specifically, "not a newer release," meant this addition "cannot
silently diverge the rest of vendor/three from the version the viewer pages were authored against" --
is now WRONG and has been removed rather than left stale: FBXLoader.js is 0.185.1 now, same as
everything else in this directory, by construction of the same single tarball fetch, not by a
separate claim that needs re-checking each round. ----

FBXLoader.js imports two things beyond three's own core, both vendored alongside it rather than
left as a dangling import: jsm/libs/fflate.module.js (101arrowz/fflate, MIT, embedded in three's own
tree at examples/jsm/libs/ -- its own header carries the MIT notice directly, a separately-authored
library three vendors rather than something three.js authors wrote) for zlib inflate on
compressed-binary FBX, and jsm/curves/NURBSCurve.js for NURBS surface support, which itself needs
jsm/curves/NURBSUtils.js. Traced by grep on every file's own `^import` lines at the 0.185.1 re-vendor,
same as at r160; the chain still terminates there -- NURBSUtils.js imports only from three's core.

NOT WIRED TO A CONVERSION PATH, TEST FIXTURE, OR GATE AT VENDORING TIME -- unchanged from the r160
note: gpu/fbxLoad.js, gpu/gpuAssetLoader.js and tools/ship/fbxIngest-selfcheck.mjs are the real
callers and are covered by this round's own gate run, not by this file.
